user_questions.question: Which refund statuses should count toward a storefront's total refunded amount? Refund__c.Status__c has Pending (default), Approved, Processing, Completed, Failed, Cancelled; IssueRefundReceiptAction creates refunds as Approved. Options: (a) Completed only - money actually paid out [recommended]; (b) Approved + Processing + Completed; (c) all except Failed and Cancelled; (d) all statuses.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Completed only: sum of Refund Amount where Status = Completed per Storefront, shown on the storefront as a new field.

skill_friction: After the user picked 'Completed', later org queries showed all three writers create refunds as 'Approved' and nothing sets 'Completed', so the total stays 0 today. SKILL.md allows 'one more message for a later intent fork' but does not say whether a discovered consequence of an already-answered question (not a new fork) warrants re-asking; I recorded it as a non-blocking open item instead.

AskCoworker D2 missed two active autolaunched flows that write Refund__c (found only via MetadataComponentDependency); the skill's 'missed components' guidance caught it but only because dependencies were checked after R/T. The workflow could say to run dependency queries on the child object before sending I.

The 'two wrong AskCoworker claims' threshold was crossed across calls (precision, Transaction__c fields, missed flows, with-sharing/ISPICKVAL proposal); unclear whether a flawed Proposal in I counts as a 'wrong claim'.

Backfill of a derived field to 0 on existing records: design-rules says derived values are filled when blank, but it is unclear whether a default-0 currency roll-up on existing parents is a required data step or optional; listed as non-blocking.

Whether lookup SetNull on parent delete fires child triggers is untestable with allowed commands; the skill says to state documented behavior precisely, but the documentation is not definitive, so the design was made defensive instead.
